items.issuing_body: U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission (as reported)
items.title: CFTC reported to have filed an emergency motion in Manhattan federal court to stop New York applying state gambling law to Kalshi
items.facts: As reported by Al Jazeera on July 31, 2026 carrying Associated Press and Reuters copy, the U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission filed an emergency motion in federal court late on Thursday night to stop New York from subjecting the prediction market Kalshi to state gambling laws, describing the state's action as overreach that would irreparably harm the agency and the markets it regulates. The same report states that the CFTC has claimed exclusive jurisdiction to regulate transactions offered in prediction markets and has challenged regulatory activity in at least nine states, including New York, which it sued in April, and that on Wednesday the federal appeals court in Manhattan rejected Kalshi's request to avoid possible enforcement activity while it appeals U.S. District Judge Analisa Torres's July 8 refusal to issue an injunction against the state. The report states that Kalshi sought to move New York's action to Manhattan federal court eight hours after the attorney general filed it, and quotes Kalshi as saying that New York seeks to place itself in the position of a nationwide derivatives regulator. PYMNTS reported the same day that the CFTC has sued to stop New York's attempt to halt Kalshi's operations, and PYMNTS and NY1 both quote CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig as stating that New York seeks to force an unprecedented sudden shutdown of prediction markets nationwide and that the CFTC has already sued to stop this and will continue to defend its jurisdiction. No official CFTC press release or public statement on this filing was located on cftc.gov, and the court filing itself was not retrieved.
items.source_label: Al Jazeera (AP and Reuters copy), July 31, 2026; corroborated by PYMNTS and NY1 (Spectrum News), July 31, 2026
items.relevant_to: prediction-market platforms, event-contract venues, designated contract markets, sportsbooks and licensed gaming operators, exchanges

items.issuing_body: New York State Office of the Attorney General
items.title: New York sues KalshiEX, LLC in state court, alleging its prediction market is an unlicensed gambling operation
items.facts: On July 31, 2026, New York Governor Kathy Hochul and Attorney General Letitia James announced that New York has sued KalshiEX, LLC for running an illegal gambling operation in New York through its prediction market platform. The Office of the Attorney General states that its investigation found Kalshi's prediction market is an illegal, unlicensed gambling operation, and that the lawsuit alleges Kalshi's prediction markets meet the legal definition of gambling because the outcomes of the events users bet on are uncertain and outside the control of the bettor or hinge on a game of chance. The release states Kalshi has failed to obtain a license from the New York State Gaming Commission, and that Kalshi's markets are available to users between the ages of 18 and 20 even though New York law requires a person to be at least 21 to participate in mobile sports betting. The Attorney General is asking the court to order Kalshi to stop operating as an unlicensed gambling business, forfeit all illegal gains, distribute restitution to consumers who were harmed, and pay fines equal to three times the gains the company made. The release notes prior related New York actions, including an October 2025 New York State Gaming Commission cease-and-desist letter to Kalshi and April 2026 suits against Coinbase and Gemini over alleged illegal gambling platforms. The matter is handled by the OAG Investor Protection Bureau.
items.source_label: New York State Office of the Attorney General press release (July 31, 2026)
items.relevant_to: prediction-market platforms, event-contract venues, sports-betting operators, crypto exchanges listing event contracts

items.issuing_body: U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission
items.title: CFTC proposes conflicts-of-interest and affiliation rules for vertically integrated market structures
items.facts: On July 30, 2026, the U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission published a Notice of Proposed Rulemaking, release 9274-26, seeking public comment on amendments to Part 37, Part 38, and Part 39 of the CFTC's regulations, as well as Commission regulations 1.52 and 1.55. The release states that the Commission has continued to observe growth in the number of affiliations between CFTC-regulated entities, including derivatives clearing organizations, designated contract markets, swap execution facilities, futures commission merchants, and other market participants such as market makers, and that in light of these developments the Commission proposes new rules and amendments to its existing regulations to address issues that may arise in connection with such firms, including with respect to perceived and potential conflicts of interest. Chairman Michael S. Selig is quoted as saying that by setting forth principles-based regulations for vertically integrated market structures, the CFTC is taking a significant step in its continued efforts to support responsible innovation in U.S. derivatives markets, and that the proposal would institute purpose-fit rules of the road that bolster market integrity without stifling novel market structures or imposing excessive compliance costs on registrants. The release states comments will be accepted for 60 days following publication in the Federal Register. As of August 2, 2026 the notice had not yet appeared in the Federal Register.
items.source_label: CFTC press release 9274-26 (July 30, 2026)
items.relevant_to: derivatives clearing organizations, designated contract markets, swap execution facilities, futures commission merchants, crypto-derivatives and prediction-market platforms

items.issuing_body: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission
items.title: SEC approves amended generic listing standards for Commodity-Based Trust Shares, adding a 15% digital-commodity buffer and allowing actively managed products
items.facts: In three orders published in the Federal Register between July 30 and August 3, 2026, the Securities and Exchange Commission approved amendments to the generic listing standards for Commodity-Based Trust Shares at Nasdaq, NYSE Arca and Cboe BZX. In Release No. 34-105995 (July 27, 2026; File No. SR-NASDAQ-2026-032), the Commission approved new Nasdaq Rule 5711(d)(iv)(C), which provides that up to 15 percent of a Commodity-Based Trust Share's net asset value in the aggregate may consist of digital commodities that do not meet the existing criteria for commodities, or securities that do not meet the existing criteria for securities, with any derivative calculated on its gross notional value. The rule defines 'digital commodity' to mean a commodity that is a digital asset and is intrinsically linked to and derives its value from the programmatic operation of a functional crypto system, as well as supply and demand dynamics, rather than from the expectation of profits from the essential managerial efforts of others. The exchanges state that this definition is informed by the joint interpretive guidance issued by the Commission and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission published at 91 FR 13714 on March 23, 2026, and that each exchange will submit a rule filing to conform the definition if legislation is enacted defining the term. The same orders remove the requirement that Commodity-Based Trust Shares be designed to reflect the performance of one or more reference assets or an index of reference assets, which permits actively managed products to be listed under the generic standards, and add a trading-halt requirement where portfolio information is not disseminated to all market participants at the same time, together with a requirement that persons with access to non-public portfolio information be subject to procedures designed to prevent its use and dissemination. At least 85 percent of net asset value must remain in assets already permitted under the standards, and the Cboe BZX order states that the sponsor must monitor compliance with the 85 percent threshold daily and promptly notify the exchange of any breach. The companion orders are Release No. 34-106001 (July 28, 2026; File No. SR-NYSEARCA-2026-42), amending NYSE Arca Rule 8.201-E (Generic), and Release No. 34-106011 (July 29, 2026; File No. SR-CboeBZX-2026-061), amending Cboe BZX Rule 14.11(e)(4).
items.source_label: Federal Register: SEC Release No. 34-105995, SR-NASDAQ-2026-032, 91 FR 48204 (July 30, 2026)

items.issuing_body: U.S. Department of the Treasury, Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC)
items.title: OFAC designates Iranian Strait of Hormuz maritime-insurance network, citing payments in digital assets used to evade sanctions
items.facts: On July 29, 2026, the U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) designated two Iran-based firms — Persian Gulf Marine Insurance Company and HormuzSafe Marine Services Authority — as part of what Treasury described as an Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC)-backed extortion scheme requiring commercial vessels to purchase mandatory maritime 'insurance' to transit the Strait of Hormuz. Treasury's press release stated that the regime 'brokers IRGC-approved policies designed to extract revenue under the guise of maritime services, including payments in digital assets to evade sanctions.' The same action added eight shipping and ship-management companies registered in Hong Kong and the Marshall Islands, and eight tankers, to OFAC's Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List under the Iran sanctions authority Executive Order 13902. Both designated Iranian firms are identified in the SDN listing as 'Organization Type: Financial and Insurance Activities' and are marked subject to secondary sanctions.
items.source_label: U.S. Treasury press release (OFAC), July 29, 2026
items.relevant_to: digital-asset exchanges, payment processors, and sanctions-compliance teams screening for OFAC-designated counterparties

items.issuing_body: U.S. District Court for the District of Minnesota
items.title: Federal judge grants Kalshi, Polymarket, and the CFTC a preliminary injunction against Minnesota's law criminalizing prediction markets
items.facts: On July 27, 2026, Judge Katherine Menendez of the U.S. District Court for the District of Minnesota granted KalshiEX LLC, Polymarket US, and the U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission a preliminary injunction against Minnesota's law criminalizing the operation of prediction markets, ruling that the plaintiffs are likely to succeed on their claim that the state law is expressly preempted by the federal Commodity Exchange Act as applied to event contracts that qualify as 'swaps.' The court wrote that plaintiffs 'have met their burden to show they are likely to succeed on the merits of their express-preemption claims, at least as to the application of Minnesota's law to many of the trades listed on Kalshi's and Polymarket US's platforms,' while noting the state ban might still reach some contracts (such as bets on entertainment outcomes) that do not qualify as swaps. The preliminary injunction remains in effect until a final decision on the merits is reached. Minnesota's law, signed May 18, 2026, was the first in the country to classify prediction-market operation as a criminal offense. As reported by CoinDesk and corroborated by the Star Tribune, NBC News, The Hill, Courthouse News Service, and other outlets.
items.source_label: CoinDesk (quoting the court's ruling)
items.relevant_to: prediction-market platforms, DCM operators, and gaming compliance teams tracking state-law bans and CEA preemption

items.issuing_body: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC)
items.title: OCC proposes information collection for GENIUS Act payment stablecoin issuer licensing applications and foreign payment stablecoin issuer registrations
items.facts: The OCC published a Paperwork Reduction Act notice (FR Doc 2026-15088; 91 FR 47032; public inspection July 24, 2026; official Federal Register publication July 27, 2026) proposing a new information collection to implement GENIUS Act licensing requirements for Permitted Payment Stablecoin Issuers (PPSIs) and registration of foreign payment stablecoin issuers. The proposed application package includes a business plan, reserve and redemption policies, a risk management program, AML/CFT compliance history, backgrounds of directors and officers, and an Interagency Biographical and Financial Report. The OCC estimates 50 respondents and 6,250 annual burden hours. The public comment period closes September 25, 2026.
items.source_label: Federal Register, FR Doc 2026-15088, 91 FR 47032
items.relevant_to: entities seeking PPSI licensing or foreign payment stablecoin issuer registration under the GENIUS Act; payment stablecoin issuers with US market access

items.issuing_body: Nevada Gaming Control Board
items.title: Kalshi Agrees to Third-Party Geofencing in Nevada Under Court Stipulation
items.facts: KalshiEX LLC and the Nevada Gaming Control Board filed a joint stipulation in Carson City District Court on July 24, 2026, cancelling a pending contempt hearing. Under the agreement, Kalshi must implement GeoComply, a third-party geolocation service, to block Nevada users from accessing sports, election, and entertainment event contracts by August 12, 2026; failure to meet the deadline triggers a $120,000 per-day fine. NGCB Chair Mike Dreitzer stated: 'This agreement will ensure that Kalshi fully complies with Nevada law moving forward, or it will face stiff penalties.'
items.source_label: Gambling Insider (reporting on Carson City District Court joint stipulation; primary document at gaming.nv.gov)

items.issuing_body: Pennsylvania General Assembly (House)
items.title: Pennsylvania HB 2711 Proposes Regulatory Framework for Prediction Markets
items.facts: On July 22, 2026, Pennsylvania Representative Tarik Khan and more than two dozen bipartisan co-sponsors introduced House Bill 2711, which would create a regulatory framework for prediction markets in Pennsylvania. The bill establishes operational standards and consumer protections including a 21-year minimum age, prohibitions on death markets and contracts involving minors, and fraud and manipulation safeguards. Enforcement authority would vest in the Pennsylvania Attorney General and local district attorneys rather than the Pennsylvania Gaming Control Board, with civil penalties up to $1 million per day for post-injunction violations. The bill does not prohibit most sports prediction markets and does not impose a revenue tax. HB 2711 was referred to the House Consumer Protection, Technology and Utilities Committee.
items.source_label: Gambling Insider (reporting on PA HB 2711; bill text at palegis.us via legiscan.com/PA/bill/HB2711/2025)
items.relevant_to: prediction-market platforms operating in or considering entry into Pennsylvania, gaming compliance and legislative monitoring teams

items.issuing_body: U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission (Division of Market Oversight)
items.title: CFTC staff advisory warns designated contract markets against broad, template-style self-certifications of event contract series
items.facts: On July 24, 2026, the U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission's Division of Market Oversight (DMO) issued an advisory reminding designated contract markets (DCMs) about the proper procedures for submitting self-certifications of an event contract series. The advisory addresses concerns about the practice of submitting broad, template-style certifications that combine many potential event contract variations into a single certification. According to the advisory, this approach limits DMO's ability to determine whether a DCM has provided all the information, explanation, and analysis required by Commission Regulation Section 40.2, and whether it has adequately evaluated the settlement methodology, data sources, and core-principles compliance of any contract it intends to list. The guidance reiterates that broad, template-style certifications should not be submitted, and explains when closely related event contracts may be certified as a class or submitted for approval under Commission Regulations Sections 40.2(d) or 40.3. The advisory was issued as CFTC Staff Letter No. 26-22.
items.source_label: CFTC Press Release 9273-26 (Division of Market Oversight advisory; CFTC Staff Letter No. 26-22) — July 24, 2026
items.relevant_to: prediction-market operators and other designated contract markets that list event contracts, and their compliance/listing teams — self-certification submissions must provide full per-contract Reg 40.2 analysis rather than broad template-style filings

items.issuing_body: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC)
items.title: OCC denies Wise's application for a US national trust bank charter, citing AML/CFT compliance deficiencies and a July 2025 multi-state consent order; Wise shares fall ~10%
items.facts: On July 24, 2026, Wise plc announced via London Stock Exchange regulatory news service (RNS) that the U.S. Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) communicated its decision to deny Wise's application for a national trust bank charter. The OCC cited significant supervisory and compliance concerns, including management's demonstrated persistent inability to manage anti-money laundering and terrorism financing risks, directors and management lacking sufficient AML/CFT experience, proposed activities presenting high AML/CFT risks, and organizers failing to demonstrate sufficient experience with banking regulations related to fiduciary activities. The OCC letter references historical issues with the original application and a multi-state consent order Wise entered into in July 2025. Wise shares fell approximately 10-11% on Nasdaq following the announcement. Wise stated it plans to submit a new application under a GENIUS Act framework. Wise's existing money transmission licenses (MTLs) across 48 US states and 4 territories are unaffected; the denial pertains solely to the proposed national trust charter. The Bank Policy Institute and banking trade groups had submitted opposition letters. The OCC's denial letter has not been separately published by the OCC on occ.gov as of this date.
items.source_label: The Defiant, 'OCC Denies Wise's US National Trust Bank Charter' — July 24, 2026 (reporting on Wise RNS announcement and Law360 review of OCC decision letter)
items.relevant_to: fintech operators seeking or considering OCC national bank or trust charters, payments and MSB operators assessing US federal licensing pathways, compliance teams tracking OCC AML-as-licensing-condition precedents in the post-GENIUS Act charter wave

items.issuing_body: U.S. Department of the Treasury / OFAC
items.title: OFAC designates 4 individuals and 9 entities supporting Iranian digital asset exchanges Zedcex and Zedxion; Istanbul fintech Zedpay and Dubai-based Zedx DMCC among designees
items.facts: On July 24, 2026, the U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) designated four individuals and nine entities that form key components of Babak Zanjani's Iranian sanctions evasion network. The action targets support infrastructure for the previously-designated digital asset exchanges Zedcex Exchange Limited and Zedxion Exchange Limited (both designated January 30, 2026). OFAC stated that multiple Zedcex and Zedxion-attributed addresses have processed funds on behalf of wallets attributed to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC). Among the newly designated entities is Istanbul-based Zedpay Finansal Sistem Ve Hizmetleri Anonim Sirketi (Zedpay), a financial technology company that provided digital wallet and global transfer services and was directly integrated into the Zedxion trading platform, giving Zedxion fiat settlement and cross-border payment capabilities. Dubai-based Zedx DMCC acted on Zedcex's behalf with regard to Zedcex's exchange wallets. Dubai-based BZ Diamond FZCO, a diamond dealer managed by Zanjani's sister Bahareh Morteza Zanjani, conducted transactions with Zedxion and Zedcex wallets and promoted Zedxion's NFT marketplace. Six Iran-based entities comprising the Dot One conglomerate are also designated, including DotOne Gold Company, which operates Tala Token (an allegedly gold-backed digital asset token); significant quantities of Tala Token passed through Zedcex infrastructure in early 2025. Designated individuals: Mehdi Rezazadeh (Zedpay chairperson, Istanbul), Sukhrob Oimakhmadov (Zedx DMCC manager, Dubai), Bahareh Morteza Zanjani (BZ Diamond FZCO manager, Dubai), and Solmaz Bani (registered websites for Zanjani companies). Designations issued pursuant to Executive Order 13902.
items.source_label: U.S. Department of the Treasury Press Release sb0576 — July 24, 2026
items.relevant_to: crypto exchanges, VASPs, fintech payment processors, banks with Turkish or UAE-based fintech integration partners — immediate SDN screening required for 13 newly-designated entities and individuals

items.issuing_body: U.S. Senate (reported)
items.title: Senate Majority Leader Thune signals CLARITY Act likely to miss pre-recess floor vote; Russia sanctions bill takes priority
items.facts: Senate Majority Leader John Thune told reporters on July 23, 2026 that the Digital Asset Market CLARITY Act is unlikely to receive a floor vote before the August 7 congressional recess, saying: 'I would like to at least get Clarity started. We'll see where the votes are.' Senate leadership plans to prioritize the Russia sanctions bill (Sen. Lindsey Graham) on the floor the following week, leaving insufficient floor time for the 60-vote cloture process. White House crypto adviser Bo Hines indicated the first week of August (Aug 1-7) may still be possible. The bill faces bipartisan opposition on the ethics provision sunset date and stablecoin yield provisions. Corroborated by Yahoo Finance, CryptoTimes, and The Defiant (all July 23, 2026). No official Senate floor schedule was published on senate.gov as of this report.
items.source_label: CoinDesk
items.relevant_to: Crypto operators, exchanges, token issuers, stablecoin issuers, and DeFi platforms planning for the federal market-structure framework — pre-recess passage now unlikely; first week of August is the remaining window before August 7 recess

items.issuing_body: U.S. Department of the Treasury / OFAC
items.title: OFAC designates Hamas money exchange El-Kahira for General Trading (Turkiye) that serviced 'both fiat and cryptocurrencies'; 7 total designees in Hamas/Muslim Brotherhood action
items.facts: On July 23, 2026, the U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) designated a senior Egyptian Muslim Brotherhood (EMB) official, along with three individuals and three entities that provided material support to Hamas. Among the designated entities is Turkiye-based El-Kahira for General Trading, which OFAC states provided underground banking services, 'servicing both fiat and cryptocurrencies,' to Hamas and to known Sweden-based organized crime groups including the Foxtrot Network. El-Kahira transferred hundreds of thousands of dollars for Hamas. El-Kahira's owner Khuldun Khamis Zakaria Alden and shareholders Zaid Issam Ahmed Al-Jebouri and Abdullah Issam Ahmad Al-Jebouri are also designated. The two other designated entities are Tujah Bulah Global (Indonesia, also known as Seven Spikes Global, a Hamas fundraising charity) and Madad Palestine Charitable Society (Gaza, a Hamas front charity whose funds were diverted to Hamas's military wing). The designated EMB official is Mahmoud al-Abyari, UK-based Secretary General of the Muslim Brotherhood General Secretariat. Designations issued pursuant to Executive Order 13224, as amended. This action follows prior Hamas/MB OFAC actions on January 21, 2026 and March 12, 2026.
items.source_label: U.S. Department of the Treasury Press Release sb0572 — July 23, 2026

items.issuing_body: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission
items.title: SEC agrees to pay $150,000 and produce records to settle Coinbase FOIA lawsuit; settlement confirms Gensler texts deleted 2022-2023 and 21 officials' phones wiped
items.facts: The SEC and History Associates Inc. (acting on behalf of Coinbase) filed a joint status report on July 22, 2026 in History Associates Inc. v. SEC (D.D.C. No. 1:24-cv-01766), settling a FOIA lawsuit over SEC records on Ethereum and Gensler-era communications. Settlement terms: SEC pays $150,000 in legal fees; SEC produces all remaining responsive documents; case dismissed upon completion. The lawsuit (filed June 2024) compelled production of thousands of SEC records. The production confirmed that SEC Chair Gensler's text messages were deleted for October 2022 through September 2023 and that 21 senior SEC officials' phones were wiped. Two previously withheld documents were released in settlement. Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong called it 'a huge win for crypto.' Reported by CoinDesk, CoinTelegraph, CryptoSlate, and FinanceFeeds (all July 23, 2026); underlying joint status report filed in PACER.
items.source_label: CoinDesk
items.relevant_to: Crypto platforms and exchanges subject to prior SEC enforcement or investigation 2022-2023; FOIA practitioners monitoring SEC records and institutional accountability

items.issuing_body: U.S. Senate (as reported)
items.title: Reported: New would-be-final CLARITY Act draft circulated July 22 with DOJ-enforced ethics ban on federal officials issuing digital assets
items.facts: As reported by CoinDesk on July 22, 2026 and corroborated by CNBC, Roll Call, American Banker and Disruption Banking the same day, lawmakers circulated a would-be-final draft of the Digital Asset Market CLARITY Act as the U.S. Senate prepared for floor action before its August recess. The draft includes a conflict-of-interest section barring the President, Vice President, members of Congress, federal judges and their spouses from issuing or sponsoring digital assets for pay while in office; per CNBC, the Department of Justice would enforce the ban with fines of up to $250,000 per day and disgorgement of profits plus a penalty of up to 10% of amounts received. The ethics provision is set to sunset January 20, 2029 and would require regulators to implement it within one year of enactment. Per CoinDesk, the draft retains the Blockchain Regulatory Certainty Act (non-custodial developers not treated as money transmitters) and adds new language on federal preemption, provisional registration and commodity pool operators. Senate Majority Leader John Thune's office said he intends to move to floor action in the coming days; the draft text was posted at Punchbowl News but had not been shared with Democratic lawmakers, several of whom criticized the DOJ-enforced ethics mechanism. The bill needs 60 Senate votes.
items.source_label: CoinDesk, July 22, 2026 (corroborated by CNBC, Roll Call, American Banker, Disruption Banking)
items.relevant_to: digital asset issuers, exchanges, DeFi developers, crypto compliance teams

items.issuing_body: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (Commissioner Hester M. Peirce)
items.title: SEC Commissioner Peirce: some crypto vaults and onchain lending strategies may fall within federal securities laws
items.facts: On July 22, 2026, SEC Commissioner Hester M. Peirce issued a statement titled 'Headstands and Summervaults: A Statement on Crypto Vaults and Lending Strategies,' stating that crypto vaults and onchain lending strategies may fall within the federal securities laws depending on how they are structured and managed. Peirce wrote that moving activities within the scope of the securities laws onchain 'as a general matter, does not take those activities outside the scope,' and that 'tokenized securities are still securities. That principle holds for vaults.' She said parties who manage vaults (for example, by selecting yield-generating activities, re-allocating assets, or selecting the parties that make those decisions) or lending strategies (for example, by setting interest rates, deciding which assets to accommodate, and setting loan-to-value limits and liquidation thresholds) may want to analyze whether their activities implicate the securities laws; that a vault could be a common enterprise or fall into investment company territory and involvement may implicate investment adviser requirements; and that onchain loans could bear the hallmarks of notes that are securities. She stated the analysis turns on the specific facts and circumstances and invited market participants to engage with the SEC. The statement is an individual Commissioner statement, not a Commission rule or enforcement action.
items.source_label: SEC.gov — Commissioner Hester M. Peirce statement, July 22, 2026
items.relevant_to: DeFi vault operators and curators, onchain lending platforms, exchanges offering stablecoin yield

items.issuing_body: U.S. House Committee on Agriculture, Subcommittee on Commodity Markets, Digital Assets, and Rural Development
items.title: House Agriculture subcommittee examines prediction market customer protections and CFTC authority over sports event contracts
items.facts: The Subcommittee on Commodity Markets, Digital Assets, and Rural Development held a hearing titled 'Examining Prediction Markets: Customer Protections and Market Integrity in Sports Event Markets' on July 21, 2026, chaired by Rep. Dusty Johnson (R-SD). Five witnesses testified: Robert Schwartz (partner, Morgan Lewis; former CFTC general counsel), Carl Kennedy (derivatives attorney, Katten Muchin Rosenman), Chris Cylke (SVP government relations, American Gaming Association), David Bean (chairman, Indian Gaming Association), and Asaf Meir (co-founder and CEO, Solidus Labs). Schwartz and Kennedy defended CFTC jurisdiction under the Commodity Exchange Act; Cylke and Bean argued sports event contracts are gambling subject to state police powers and the Indian Gaming Regulatory Act, with Bean urging advancement of H.R. 7840 (Event Contract Enforcement Act). Cylke cited Kalshi's sports-related trading volume exceeding $111 billion through H1 2026 and noted that 45% of all online sports betting advertising now comes from prediction market operators. Rep. Kristen McDonald Rivet (D-MI) pressed witnesses on the CFTC's order directing Kalshi to defy a Michigan state court order; Schwartz described the order as extraordinary, stating: 'It certainly was a flex.' Rep. Angie Craig (D-MN) questioned whether a single-commissioner CFTC had the capability to police prediction markets given proposed budget cuts. Chairman Johnson closed by stating: 'Courts are acting in this space. The commission is acting in this space. I do not think that this committee, Congress, should be silent. We have an obligation to drive toward finding out what is the common ground.' Testimony documents are posted at agriculture.house.gov.
items.source_label: House Agriculture Committee hearing page, July 21, 2026

items.issuing_body: Washington State Office of the Attorney General / King County Superior Court
items.title: Washington State Court Grants Preliminary Injunction Against Kalshi for Violations of State Gambling Act and Consumer Protection Act
items.facts: King County Superior Court (Washington state) granted a preliminary injunction against Kalshi on July 20, 2026, finding that Kalshi's prediction market contracts likely violate both the Washington Gambling Act and the Consumer Protection Act. The court found that Kalshi's event contracts — covering sports, elections, natural disasters, and other contingent events — constitute gambling under Washington law, which defines gambling as staking or risking something of value upon the outcome of a contest of chance or a future contingent event, and prohibits internet gambling as amended in 2006. The court also ruled that Kalshi's marketing constitutes unfair and deceptive acts or practices under the Consumer Protection Act, citing a Kalshi advertisement in which a user texts about finding 'a way to bet on the NFL even though we live in Washington.' Washington AG Nick Brown filed the underlying complaint on March 27, 2026. The court will issue a final injunction order setting full remedies on August 5, 2026. Washington is reported as the 4th state to obtain a preliminary injunction against Kalshi's sports event contracts, with state regulators and courts prevailing in 19 of 23 such decisions nationally.

items.issuing_body: Federal Trade Commission
items.title: FTC: Celsius Network founders to pay $16.5 million; banned from marketing asset deposit and withdrawal products
items.facts: The FTC announced on July 20, 2026 that Alexander Mashinsky, former CEO of cryptocurrency platform Celsius Network Inc., and business partners Shlomi Daniel Leon and Hanoch "Nuke" Goldstein will pay a total of $16.5 million to resolve FTC charges that they deceived users by falsely promising that deposits made to their cryptocurrency platform would be safe and always available. Mashinsky pays $10 million, Leon $4.1 million and Goldstein $2.4 million. Mashinsky and Leon also agreed to a ban on marketing or selling products or services that can be used to deposit, exchange, invest or withdraw assets; Goldstein agreed to a ban covering retail products or services used to buy, sell, deposit, withdraw, distribute or trade cryptocurrency. The orders, filed in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York, also prohibit misrepresentations about any product or service and violations of the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act. The Commission vote on the Mashinsky order was 3-0; the votes on the Leon and Goldstein orders were 2-0.

items.issuing_body: Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation
items.title: FDIC publishes GENIUS Act PPSI reporting forms for PRA comment (FR Doc. 2026-14589, 91 FR 45274)
items.facts: On July 20, 2026 (filed on public inspection July 17), the FDIC published a Paperwork Reduction Act notice (FR Doc. 2026-14589, 91 FR 45274) requesting 60-day public comment on proposed weekly and quarterly reporting forms for FDIC-supervised Permitted Payment Stablecoin Issuers (PPSIs). The notice is associated with the FDIC's GENIUS Act PPSI NPRM (April 10, 2026, 91 FR 18534). Weekly Form PS-01 (for PPSIs with $1 billion or more in total outstanding issuance value or $100 million or more in average daily transaction volume) includes eight schedules covering top holders, top exchanges, trading volume, top counterparties, capital, issuance and redemption, and reserve assets disaggregated by type (cash and deposits, U.S. Treasuries by CUSIP, reverse repurchase agreements, money market mutual funds, and other instruments). Weekly Form PS-01a (smaller PPSIs) has three schedules. Quarterly Form PS-02 covers income statement, balance sheet, off-balance sheet items, capital and operational backstop, and memoranda including blockchain activity, redemption metrics, and custody activities. The FDIC estimates approximately 30 FDIC-supervised institutions would perform PPSI activities; ongoing weekly reporting burden estimated at 2,080 hours per year and quarterly at 800 hours. The publication confirms the FDIC GENIUS Act implementing final rule was not published as of the July 18, 2026 statutory one-year deadline. Comment period closes September 18, 2026.

items.issuing_body: Federal Reserve Board
items.title: Fed Chair Warsh testifies to House Financial Services: no Federal Reserve bailout for crypto or stablecoins; Fed 'racing' to meet GENIUS Act stablecoin rulemaking deadline; nonbank fintech payment access pressed
items.facts: Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh testified before the House Committee on Financial Services on July 14, 2026, as part of the Semiannual Monetary Policy Report (2128 Rayburn House Office Building, 10:00 AM). The official prepared statement focused on price stability, monetary policy, and internal Fed task forces. During the Q&A, Warsh made three statements directly relevant to crypto, stablecoin, and fintech operators: (1) No Federal Reserve bailout for crypto or stablecoins: Pressed by Rep. Brad Sherman on whether the Fed would provide the kind of support it gave money market funds in 2008, Warsh stated 'We do not want to be in the bailout business, full stop.' He added that the Fed would 'do everything we can to mitigate... extraordinary risks' but would not bail out crypto. He did not fully rule out marginal systemic-spillover mitigation. (2) GENIUS Act rulemaking urgency: Warsh told lawmakers the Fed is 'racing' to finalize its portion of the GENIUS Act stablecoin implementing rules ahead of the July 18, 2026 one-year statutory deadline. The deadline has since been confirmed missed (the Federal Register contains no in-scope publication; July 18 is a Saturday; earliest possible publication is Monday July 20). (3) Nonbank fintech payment-system access: Rep. Sherman separately pressed on Kraken's pending bank application and nonbank crypto firms seeking direct access to the payment system; Warsh invoked systemic-risk considerations without making a specific commitment. Background: Warsh is the most crypto-sympathetic Fed Chair on record, having previously disclosed venture stakes in Bitcoin payments, a crypto index manager, Bitwise, and a stablecoin venture â all divested under Fed ethics rules prior to confirmation in May 2026. A 2026 New York Fed staff report cited in contemporaneous coverage found stablecoin activity can transmit liquidity stress to banks and complicate monetary policy. This is Warsh's first congressional testimony since his confirmation. Secondary coverage: Law360, July 14, 2026 ('Fed Racing To Hit Genius Act Rules Deadline, Warsh Says'); CCN via Yahoo Finance, July 15, 2026 ('Fed Chair Kevin Warsh Says Crypto and Stablecoins Are On Their Own in a Crisis').

items.title: ICBA, ABA and 76 state banking associations urge Senate leaders to tighten CLARITY Act Section 404 stablecoin yield provisions
items.facts: As announced by the Independent Community Bankers of America on July 13, 2026, the American Bankers Association and ICBA, joined by 76 state associations, sent a letter to Senate Majority Leader John Thune and Minority Leader Charles Schumer urging targeted changes to the CLARITY Act to provide greater certainty that payment stablecoins cannot function as substitutes for bank deposits. The associations wrote that 'significant questions remain regarding whether the current language in Section 404 provides sufficient clarity and certainty to achieve that objective' and that 'ambiguities within the bill could encourage stablecoin arrangements to effectively function as substitutes for deposits, despite Congress's longstanding and clearly stated intent that payment stablecoins should serve as transaction tools rather than store-of-value products.' They urge revisions clarifying the prohibition on interest and yield, replacing the bill's 'functional and economic equivalent' standard with a 'substantially similar' standard, and removing language they believe could create ambiguity regarding rewards tied to stablecoin balances, duration or tenure. items.issuing_body: Arizona Department of Gaming
items.title: Arizona Department of Gaming issues cease-and-desist orders to five online gambling operators alleging felony promotion of gambling, illegal control of an enterprise, and money laundering
items.facts: On July 10, 2026, the Arizona Department of Gaming announced it had issued cease-and-desist orders to BetOpenly, Bookmaker, Club WPT Online Poker, Kutt Inc., and Raffle Creator, with each enforcement action alleging conduct giving rise to the felonies of promotion of gambling, illegal control of an enterprise, and money laundering. The Department alleges, among other things, that BetOpenly enabled event wagering and daily fantasy sports contests without the requisite state licenses and facilitated availability to underage Arizonans; that Bookmaker facilitated wagering on horse racing, casino games, and sports betting without an event wagering or advanced deposit wagering provider license; that Club WPT Online Poker enabled Arizonans under 21 to engage in pay-to-play online poker tournaments for prizes while using deceptive 'no purchase necessary' language; that Kutt Inc. allowed Arizona users to deposit money and wager on sports, politics, pop culture and casino-style games in a manner providing prohibited third-party benefit; and that Raffle Creator allowed people under 21 to purchase raffle tickets for prizes without meeting Arizona nonprofit raffle requirements. Notified entities are directed to immediately stop all gambling operations and activities in Arizona and to desist from future illegal gambling operations; the Department states future actions may include criminal charges or civil action against entities, principals, and employees, potential restitution awards, and forfeiture of all monies acquired due to the illegal conduct. Department Director Jackie Johnson said, 'Through these cease-and-desist orders we are putting operators on notice: their conduct runs contrary to Arizona law and they must stop promoting illegal gambling.' All conduct described is alleged by the Department and unadjudicated.

items.issuing_body: North Carolina Office of the Governor
items.title: North Carolina Governor Stein signs $34B SB 257 budget enacting 6% prediction-market tax on net trading-fee revenue, effective 2027
items.facts: On July 8, 2026, North Carolina Governor Josh Stein signed Senate Bill 257, the state's approximately $34 billion fiscal year 2026 budget. items.issuing_body: U.S. Supreme Court
items.title: SCOTUS rules 6-3 that for-cause removal protections for SEC and CFTC commissioners are unconstitutional (Trump v. Slaughter, No. 25-332)
items.facts: On June 29, 2026, the Supreme Court of the United States issued its 6-3 opinion in Trump v. Slaughter (No. 25-332), authored by Chief Justice Roberts, overturning Humphrey's Executor v. United States (1935). The Court held that the for-cause removal protection in the FTC's enabling statute — and by structural extension the SEC and CFTC, which operate under identical removal provisions — is contrary to the separation of powers under the Constitution. Effective immediately, the President may remove SEC and CFTC commissioners without cause. A companion order in Trump v. Cook (No. 25A312, June 29, 2026) denied a government application to stay a preliminary injunction protecting Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook; the Federal Reserve's statutory structure was not directly addressed by the majority opinion. The opinion is published on the Court's official slip opinion list for October Term 2025.
items.source_label: U.S. Supreme Court — Official Slip Opinion List, October Term 2025 (primary source; retrieved July 3, 2026); Opinion PDF: https://www.supremecourt.gov/opinions/25pdf/25-322_new_4gcj.pdf

items.title: Five federal agencies propose a customer identification program rule for payment stablecoin issuers (GENIUS Act)
items.facts: On June 18, 2026, the Federal Reserve Board — jointly with the OCC, FDIC, NCUA, and Treasury/FinCEN — requested comment on a proposed rule requiring permitted payment stablecoin issuers (PPSIs) to maintain an effective customer identification program (CIP). Comments are due 60 days after publication in the Federal Register.
items.source_label: Federal Reserve Board Press Release (June 18, 2026); joint with OCC, FDIC, NCUA, and Treasury/FinCEN.
items.relevant_to: payment stablecoin issuers (PPSIs), crypto exchanges and custodians, banks and credit unions entering stablecoins, BSA/AML and compliance teams

items.issuing_body: State of Illinois (Gov. JB Pritzker)
items.title: Illinois enacts first-in-nation digital-asset transaction tax (SB 3019 / Digital Asset Tax Act)
items.facts: Illinois Governor JB Pritzker signed Senate Bill 3019, the Digital Asset Tax Act (DATA), as part of the state's $55.9 billion budget, making Illinois the first U.S. state to impose a transaction-based tax on digital-asset activity. The law imposes a 0.2% privilege tax on brokers who exchange, transfer, or store digital assets for customers in the state; takes effect January 1, 2027.
items.source_label: Crypto Briefing (reporting Illinois SB 3019; signing also reported by Yahoo Finance, Bitcoin Magazine, The Defiant)
items.relevant_to: crypto exchanges, brokers, custodians and wallet providers with Illinois nexus; payment processors; tax/compliance teams

items.issuing_body: U.S. Senate Banking Committee (Congress)
items.title: Congress folds a statutory Fed CBDC ban (through 2030) into the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act (H.R. 6644)
items.facts: On June 16, 2026, the leaders of the Senate Banking and House Financial Services Committees released updated bill text for H.R. 6644, folding in a statutory ban on a Federal Reserve CBDC through December 31, 2030.
items.source_label: U.S. Senate Banking Committee Press Release (June 16, 2026)
items.relevant_to: stablecoin issuers, payment and fintech platforms, banks, digital-dollar infrastructure providers

items.issuing_body: Tribal Amici (coalition of federally recognized tribes)
items.title: Tribal coalition files amicus briefs opposing CFTC/Kalshi preemption of tribal gaming laws
items.facts: A coalition of federally recognized tribes filed amicus briefs in two federal prediction-market cases, arguing that allowing Kalshi and the CFTC to override state gaming laws would also nullify tribal-state gaming compacts.
items.source_label: The Defiant (reporting the Tribal Amici amicus briefs; corroborated by Protos)
items.relevant_to: prediction-market / event-contract platforms, tribal gaming operators, sportsbooks, exchanges

items.issuing_body: U.S. District Court, W.D. Michigan
items.title: W.D. Michigan denies Polymarket PI — court rules sports event contracts are NOT 'swaps' under the CEA; CEA may not preempt state gambling law even if they were
items.facts: On June 17, 2026, the W.D. Michigan denied Polymarket's motion for a preliminary injunction against enforcement of Michigan state gambling law. The court held: (1) sports event contracts are not 'swaps' under the CEA; and (2) even if they were swaps, it is not clearly established that the CEA would preempt Michigan's state gambling law.
items.source_label: SBC Americas (reporting the W.D. Michigan PI denial)
items.relevant_to: prediction-market platforms, event-contract operators, state gaming regulators, sportsbooks

items.issuing_body: NYDFS
items.title: NYDFS proposes stablecoin regulation aligning New York's framework with the federal GENIUS Act
items.facts: On June 9, 2026, the New York State Department of Financial Services, under Acting Superintendent Kaitlin Asrow, proposed a regulation to build on New York's existing stablecoin framework and align it with the federal GENIUS Act.
items.source_label: NYDFS Press Release (June 9, 2026)
items.relevant_to: stablecoin issuers, virtual-currency (BitLicense) licensees, custodians, payment-stablecoin platforms

items.issuing_body: CFTC
items.title: CFTC issues Request for Information on fintech innovation, AI, and digital asset technologies (Release 9254-26)
items.facts: On June 16, 2026, the CFTC issued Release 9254-26, a Request for Information on fintech innovation, AI, and digital asset technologies. The RFI covers DeFi protocols, AI/ML applications in trading, RWA tokenization, payment stablecoins as margin/collateral, and cybersecurity.
items.source_label: CFTC Press Release 9254-26
items.relevant_to: DeFi protocols, crypto exchanges, stablecoin issuers, AI trading firms, RWA tokenization platforms

items.issuing_body: Pennsylvania Supreme Court
items.title: Pennsylvania Supreme Court rules skill games are slot machines; 120-day enforcement stay issued
items.facts: On June 15, 2026, the Pennsylvania Supreme Court issued its majority opinion in J-97-2025 (Pace-O-Matic v. Pennsylvania), ruling that skill game machines 'are subject to both the Gaming Act and the Crimes Code,' overturning a Commonwealth Court ruling. The Court issued a 120-day enforcement stay.
items.source_label: Pennsylvania Supreme Court Opinion J-97-2025 (majority opinion)
items.relevant_to: skill game operators, gaming venues (bars, VFWs, fraternal clubs), payment processors, PA legislators

items.issuing_body: Financial Technology Association v. Tennessee — Davidson County Chancery Court
items.title: Fintech trade group sues Tennessee to block remittance tax (HB2502)
items.facts: The Financial Technology Association filed suit in Davidson County (Tennessee) Chancery Court seeking an injunction to block HB2502, a law signed by Gov. Bill Lee in May 2026 that adds a $10 fee on monetary wire transfers abroad plus a 2% tax on transfers over $500 (effective Jan. 1, 2027). The FTA argues the law is unconstitutional under the dormant Commerce Clause.
items.source_label: The Center Square (reporting the FTA v. Tennessee filing)
items.relevant_to: money transmitters, remittance providers, payment processors, fintechs

items.issuing_body: Delaware General Assembly (HB 441) / New Jersey Legislature (S-2141)
items.title: Delaware (HB 441) and New Jersey (S-2141) advance statewide crypto-ATM bans
items.facts: Delaware and New Jersey have each advanced legislation to ban cryptocurrency ATMs statewide, citing fraud losses. Delaware's HB 441 passed the House; it would require existing kiosks to go dark upon enactment and be physically removed within 90 days. New Jersey's S-2141 cleared the Senate Commerce Committee unanimously.
items.source_label: The Defiant (reporting the Delaware and New Jersey crypto-ATM ban bills)
items.relevant_to: crypto-ATM/kiosk operators, payment processors, compliance vendors

items.issuing_body: Gary Gensler (amicus) — U.S. Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit
items.title: Gensler files Sixth Circuit amicus arguing sports prediction markets are not 'swaps'
items.facts: On 2026-06-11, former CFTC and SEC chair Gary Gensler filed an amicus brief with the Sixth Circuit in KalshiEx LLC v. Schuler, arguing that sports-event prediction-market contracts fall outside the statutory definition of a 'swap' under Dodd-Frank and are therefore not within the CFTC's exclusive jurisdiction.
items.source_label: The Defiant (reporting the Gensler Sixth Circuit amicus brief)
items.relevant_to: prediction-market platforms, derivatives exchanges, crypto exchanges

items.issuing_body: State of Wisconsin (Attorney General) — U.S. District Court, W.D. Wis.
items.title: Wisconsin moves to block sports event-contract trading on Coinbase, Kalshi, and Robinhood
items.facts: On 2026-06-09, the State of Wisconsin filed a motion for a preliminary injunction seeking to block KalshiEx, Coinbase, and Robinhood from offering sports event-contract trading to people in the state.
items.source_label: DeFi Rate (reporting the Wisconsin preliminary-injunction motion)
items.relevant_to: prediction-market platforms, crypto exchanges, brokerages

items.issuing_body: Coalition for Fair Markets (NADEX, Kalshi, Polymarket/QCX)
items.title: Prediction-market coalition sues Kentucky over 14.25% tax on event-contract trading
items.facts: On 2026-06-12, the Coalition for Fair Markets — comprising Crypto.com's NADEX, Kalshi, and Polymarket's U.S. exchange QCX — filed suit in Franklin Circuit Court to block Kentucky from implementing a 14.25% tax on prediction-market transaction fees set to take effect Jan. 1, 2027.
items.source_label: SBC Americas (reporting the Coalition for Fair Markets filing; first reported by the Associated Press)
items.relevant_to: prediction-market platforms, licensed gaming operators, payment processors

items.issuing_body: Nevada Gaming Control Board
items.title: Nevada gaming regulator seeks to hold Kalshi in contempt over prediction-market geofencing
items.facts: On 2026-06-12 the Nevada Gaming Control Board petitioned the First Judicial District Court in Carson City to find KalshiEx LLC in contempt for allegedly not complying with a May 18 order requiring it to geofence its website so it cannot offer sports-, election-, or entertainment-related event contracts to anyone located in Nevada.
items.source_label: Las Vegas Review-Journal (reporting the Nevada GCB court filing)
items.relevant_to: prediction-market platforms, geolocation/compliance vendors, sportsbooks

items.issuing_body: CFTC
items.title: CFTC sues New Mexico over prediction-market preemption (8th state)
items.facts: On 2026-06-12 the CFTC filed suit against the State of New Mexico, seeking a declaratory judgment that federal law grants it exclusive authority over event contracts and a permanent injunction barring the state from enforcing preempted gaming laws against CFTC registrants. New Mexico joins AZ, CT, IL, NY, MN, RI, and WI.
items.source_label: CFTC Press Release 9251-26
items.relevant_to: prediction-market platforms, sportsbooks, exchanges, CFTC registrants
